foot: Payments recorded here gate the next order at entry — the loop is live.

blocks.v: 1 · Getting started
Sign in
Open hq.healthspan.ph in any browser (Safari, Chrome — phone, iPad, or computer).
Enter your Healthspan email and password. Tick Remember me on your own device; leave it unticked on shared computers.
Forgot your password? Ask an admin — they can set a new one in seconds. You can change it anytime via the password link at the bottom of the sidebar.
Install it as an app (do this once)
On iPhone/iPad: open hq.healthspan.ph in Safari → tap Share → Add to Home Screen.
On Android: open it in Chrome → menu ⋮ → Add to Home screen.
It now opens full-screen like a real app, with the Healthspan icon.

Make the bottom bar yours: Menu → ☆ Customize bar — pick the pages you use most for one-tap access. Home and Menu are always there (specialists also keep Log visit and New order fixed, with 2 free slots; everyone else picks 4).
Your favourites
Star any page from the ☆ in the top bar. It pins to the top of the sidebar, directly under Home, and to the top of your home page — one list, both places, so there is nothing to keep in sync.
Prefer to set them all at once? Choose favourites — the edit link on the home row, or Menu → Choose favourites on a phone — opens the full picker. Up to 10.
The Favourites heading in the sidebar collapses and expands like every other section, and remembers which way you left it.
They are yours, on this device, the same as the bottom bar — and only pages your role can open are ever offered.
Sorting any table

Click any column heading to sort A–Z; click it again for Z–A. It works on every table in HQ. Money, quantities, dates and expiry months sort by their real value, not alphabetically, and blank cells always go to the bottom. Section headings and TOTAL lines stay put. The sort lasts until the page redraws — it is a way to look at what is on screen, not a saved setting.
When a page refreshes

After you do something — add a line, submit a form, approve, release — the page updates in place. It does not blank out or jump back to the top; whatever you were looking at stays put while the new numbers land. You only see a "Loading" message when you open a page for the first time.
Attaching files

Where you see + Attach, you can add files straight from your phone or computer — photos, quotations, receipts, signed slips. They are stored in the Healthspan Google Drive, and opening one goes back through HQ, so your access here decides what you can see. Anything over about 4 MB opens in Drive instead. Remove a file with the ✕ beside it.
On a pull-out request: the register row underneath the form.
On any of the seven finance forms: the register row that appears once you submit — quotations, receipts, bank approvals, BIR forms.
A file can only be removed by whoever uploaded it (or by whoever runs that area). Removing it deletes it from Drive too, so the ✕ asks first.
The bell

The bell at the top pings you when the system needs you — a red badge shows unread items. Tap it to see what happened and jump straight to the right page. It checks for news every 90 seconds. What pings whom is listed at the end of this manual.
Ask AI

The Ask AI button answers plain-language questions over everything HQ knows — inventory, sales, receivables, cheques, approvals, backorders, quotes, pipeline — and its knowledge is automatically scoped to YOUR role: specialists get their own numbers, costs and margins only answer for finance and admin. Any hour, in the app or on Slack (/stock).
Your manual & view-only pages

The manual link at the bottom of the sidebar (phone: Menu → My manual) opens this manual INSIDE the app — read it there, download it, or pop it full screen. And wherever a page is read-only for your role, a banner at the top says so and names who actually edits it; the same pages carry a small “VIEW” badge on your home screen.
You also hold the circle read: sales analytics, inventory value, pipeline — live.
TIP — Every number view has a plain-language description at the top and a “how is this calculated” section — read those before asking. Most views also export to CSV.
Home, navigation & everyday mechanics

Home is the command center: live stat chips (orders today, pending, open follow-ups…), a needs-attention line, and big launcher cards for your role. It updates in place while the data syncs — no flicker, no reload.
Sidebar search: type in the box at the top of the sidebar to filter every menu item; sections collapse and remember their state (Product lines starts collapsed).
Every page has a real URL: bookmark an account, an order, a pick list; the browser back button works; share links with teammates — they’ll see it with THEIR permissions.
Mobile: the bottom bar carries your essentials; the Menu button reaches every view, plus password change, sign-out, and theme.
Themes: Healthspan (brand blue, light/dark/system) or Classic — bottom of the sidebar.
Data freshness: the sheet syncs every 15 minutes; Shopify nightly at 2am; the footer shows the last sync. “Refresh” forces one.
My profile — your own page
My profile sits right under Home in the sidebar; tapping your name in the footer or the phone menu opens it too.

It shows who you are signed in as, every finance form you have filed and where each one stands, your open follow-ups and this month’s visits (if you carry a specialist tag, with a jump to your full sales page), any loaners you checked out, and the quick actions — password, manual, favourites.

On a phone or iPad, a small ← sits in the top bar whenever there is somewhere to go back to — and swiping right from the left edge of the screen does the same. At the bottom of the history it takes you Home.
Period close — what freezes when a month is signed off

Once accounting has signed a month off, the super admin closes it on the Cutover switches page. From then on, everything dated on or before the cut-off is frozen: order amounts, order dates, order lines, credit memos, cheque maturities and that month’s targets.

What still works inside a closed month: recording a payment (a July invoice paid in September is September cash), marking shipments dispatched or delivered, picking and fulfilling, and assigning a DR number. Those are operational, not revenue-changing.

What is refused: changing an order’s amount, date or lines; cancelling, trashing or restoring it; back-dating an open order into the closed month; deleting a cheque; editing a closed month’s target. If a closed sale needs reversing, record a credit memo — which is the accounting-correct move anyway.
Why you cannot work around it: the rule lives in the database, not the screen. The app warns you first as a courtesy, but even a faulty page or a background job cannot rewrite a closed month.
Reopening is the same control and only the super admin has it — it warns exactly what is being unlocked.
Receivables: AR aging, payments, statements
AR aging: every open balance bucketed current / 1–30 / 31–60 / 60+ past terms (order date + terms days). Oldest debts flag red. Terms are parsed from order notes (“PDC 30 days”) or set on the order.
Recording payments (order page, native orders): amount → paid/partial/pending recalculates; balances feed AR, credit checks, and the cash-flow forecast instantly.
Migrated Shopify orders sync payment status nightly from Shopify (totalOutstanding is truth there until cutover) — record those in Shopify.
Statements: printable per-account Statement of Account — every order, paid, balance, terms, plus the aging summary. One click from the account page.
THE LOOP — The balance you record is what order entry checks on that account’s NEXT order. Delayed bookkeeping = a blind credit gate.
Recording a payment — with its own date
On any order page, record payment asks for the amount, the date received, and a method or reference (bank transfer, cheque number).
The date matters: it decides which month the cash belongs to, independently of when the invoice was raised.
Payments are append-only — there is no edit or delete. A wrong entry is corrected by recording an offsetting negative amount, so the trail always shows what really happened.
The order’s paid/balance figures remain the running total, and AR aging reads them as before.

Collections CSV on AR aging lists the individual dated payments for a period — what actually came in, by day. Payments recorded before this feature existed have no date and appear only in the order totals.
PDC register
Every post-dated cheque: account, order ref, bank, cheque no., amount, maturity date, status.
Statuses: on hand → deposited → cleared (or bounced). Due cheques highlight as maturity approaches.
Cards up top: deposit-this-week, arriving-in-30-days — the register feeds the cash-flow forecast automatically.
Cash-flow forecast
8 weekly buckets of expected collections: AR lands in the week its terms mature; cheques land in the week they can be deposited.
Accounts with a cheque in hand count ONCE — via the cheque, not the invoice.
The red card = overdue money with no cheque: that is the chase list. “Beyond 8 weeks” holds long terms and far maturities.
Bars show the relative size of each week at a glance.
Returns & credit memos
Record the return against its order: lines, quantities, and restock vs write-off per line.
It gets a permanent CM number and a printable credit memo with the VAT split.
Apply to order balance (admin) settles the memo against what the clinic owes.
Parallel-run banner: process the refund in Shopify too until cutover — this register becomes the only one after.
Credit limits & commissions
Credit limits — you hold the gate
Set the credit limit on any account page (finance + admin).
From then on: a specialist order that would push (open balance + new total) past the limit holds automatically for manager approval. You can watch decisions in the Approvals view.
The nightly sweep also pings you (and the account owner) when any account crosses 60 days past terms.
Commissions
Tiered %-of-target rules — default: <80% → 0% · 80% → 1% · 100% → 2% · 120% → 3%. Edit as “min:pct” lines; changes apply immediately and are audited.
Monthly compute per specialist: booked vs their target → attainment → tier → commission.
Export CSV — payroll-ready.
Pull-out requests — stock for internal use

Logistics → Pull-out requests. Anything leaving the warehouse that is not a sale — KOL engagements, brand campaigns, FOC promos, trade partnerships, launches and training — goes through here. It replaces the Google pull-out form, and unlike the form it actually holds the stock.

File a request (anyone with a login): pick the products from the catalogue — you see on-hand and available-to-promise beside each one — then quantity and unit, the fund source (the QBO class that pays for it), the reason, the product line, the date needed, and what it is for.

Submitting reserves the units immediately. They drop out of available-to-promise, so nobody can sell the same box while your request is pending. If there is not enough available you are warned but can still submit — the warehouse sees the shortfall.

The fund source approves. Only the person mapped to that class (or their named backup) can decide, and they are pinged the moment it lands. Approval notifies finance and the warehouse; a rejection comes back to you with the reason and frees the stock.

If you are an approver, the page opens with a banner naming the classes you own and what is waiting on you. Your approval rights come from the fund-source list, not from your access level — several approvers hold view-only access everywhere else in HQ and still approve their class normally.
The warehouse releases the goods — and that is the only step that moves stock: earliest-expiry-first, batch-stamped against the PL number, so a pulled lot is as traceable as a sold one.
Mark booked: during the parallel run the specialist still records it in Shopify; tick it here with the reference so nothing is left half-done.
Pull-outs are internal issues — they never count as sales, anywhere.
Fund-source spend — the class charge
On the same page, finance and admin get the money view of pull-outs.

Per class, per month: how many requests, how many units, the value at item-master cost (the basis QBO wants for a class charge — not list price), how many have been released and how many are still open.

Export for QBO gives one row per line item: pull-out number, date, status, class, reason, product line, who requested, who approved, SKU, quantity, unit cost, value, release date, booking reference and purpose.

Rejected and cancelled requests are excluded. Lines with no cost on the item master are flagged rather than quietly counted as zero — if that number is not zero, the item master needs costs before the figures can be trusted.
Released rows have physically left the warehouse; still-open ones are reserved but not yet handed over.
Finance forms

Seven forms live under Finance forms: pull-out requests, voucher for approval, request to order/pay, proof of payment, request for replenishment, expense reimbursement, and request for cash advance. They replace the Google forms and behave the same way as each other.
Anyone with a login can file one. Fill it in, submit, then attach the supporting documents to the row that appears in the register underneath — quotations, receipts, bank approvals, BIR forms.

Some sections appear only when they apply. Choosing “Pay” on a request to order/pay shows the supplier and bank fields; choosing “Order” shows the item rows instead. Only what you can see is submitted.

It then moves through approval steps set for that form. The register shows which step each request is on and who it is waiting for. You are told when yours is approved or rejected, and rejection always comes with the reason.
Nobody approves their own request — if you are the approver for a class and you file against it yourself, it goes to someone else.
You can cancel your own request while it is still pending, and nothing else about it.
Each form has its own number — V- for vouchers, RO- for requests to order/pay, PP- proofs of payment, RP- replenishments, RE- reimbursements, CA- cash advances, PL- pull-outs.

Who sees what: these carry bank details and personal claims, so the register is not open to everyone. You see your own requests, any waiting on your decision, and finance and admin see all of them. Attachments follow the same rule.
Expense reports — liquidating a revolving fund

For whoever holds a revolving fund. Finance forms → Expense report: the period covered, then one line per receipt — date, category, description, amount. The total must equal the lines, and every receipt attaches to the register row.

It gets an ER- number and moves through the approval steps set for this form, like every finance form. Approval clears the way to top the fund back up — that stays its own filing, the Request for replenishment.
Option lists and approval routes

Option lists (finance and admin) hold the dropdowns behind the forms: event codes, cash-flow tags, product lines, payment modes, replenishment and reimbursement types, teams. Add a code when a programme starts. Retire rather than delete when one ends — historical requests keep reading correctly, the code just stops appearing on new forms. Renaming a code changes it on existing requests too, because they store the code itself.

Approval routes (admin) set who signs off which form, in order. A step can point at a named person, at anyone holding a role — which survives someone leaving — or at the request’s own fund source, so marketing spend goes to the marketing approver without needing a step each.
A step can carry a minimum amount, so small claims skip it and only larger ones need the extra signature.
Pull-out requests are the exception: they route straight off the fund-source table, not this one.
Supplier bills / AP
On every purchase order: terms · proforma ref · currency · FX total · amount paid · peso value — editable by finance.
The open-payables card totals what’s owed across POs — the weekly Inventory AP table, generated.
Supplier bill PAYMENTS stay in the bank portals/QBO by design; HQ tracks the obligations.
Suppliers, imports & multi-currency

Supplier master (Logistics → Suppliers & imports): every supplier with currency, payment terms, lead time in days, and contacts. Lead times sharpen ordering judgment — the forecast assumes ~2 months when unset.
On the water: every ordered/partial PO with an ETA, sorted soonest-first, with its customs status pill.
Import tracking per PO: ETD, ETA, customs status (in transit / clearing / cleared / delivered), and broker — edited right on the purchase order.
Multi-currency: the PO carries its currency, invoice total, amount paid, and the FX rate at payment — which converts foreign costs into real ₱ for the valuation page.
QA hold at receiving: when booking a delivery in, choose SELLABLE (straight to the ledger) or QA HOLD (quarantined until inspection releases it — released units enter the ledger as receives).
Receiving & supplier scorecard — did we get what we ordered?
Logistics → Receiving & supplier score. Every purchase order already records units ordered and units received; this page finally reads them.
Fill rate: units received divided by units ordered, per supplier — graded green at 98%+, red below 75%.
On time: deliveries that landed on or before the ETA.

Lead time: the real number (PO created → fully received) sitting next to the lead time the supplier quotes us. Where the real number runs 25%+ past quoted, the reorder plan is quietly under-buying and the supplier’s lead time is worth updating.
Receiving discrepancies: every line on a closed PO where received did not equal ordered, valued at PO cost. Short ships are claimable against the supplier; over-ships need a costing decision.
Landed cost & valuation (costs page — admin + finance only)

Unit cost per SKU = the latest PO receive cost (× the payment FX rate for foreign POs) + that PO’s landed cost (freight + customs + brokerage) spread across its received units; falls back to the item-master cost.
Real margins: each SKU’s margin vs its VAT-inclusive list price — red under 30%, amber under 50%.
Inventory at cost: what the stock is actually worth, in total and by product line, next to its value at list — the blended margin in one glance.
This page never renders for other roles — it is THE costs page.
Month-end valuation snapshots
The valuation page recomputes from today’s costs and today’s stock — which means “inventory value at 31 July” quietly changes every time somebody edits a cost. Freezing fixes the number in place.
Freeze on Landed cost & valuation stores that month’s value, units, SKU count, which stock truth was live, and the per-SKU detail.
The snapshot history sits on the same page, so you can show accounting a permanent figure.
Do it once a month, after the count and before the sign-off. On the 1st the bell reminds you if last month is still unfrozen.
Re-freezing a month that already has a snapshot is a super-admin decision — the first figure is the one accounting saw.
Accounting export & the QBO handoff

Any date range as CSV: totals, VAT 12% breakdown (prices VAT-inclusive; net = ÷1.12), payments, balances, terms. Pull-outs and TEST orders are excluded from sales everywhere but retained for logistics. “Vs accounting” reconciles HQ to the official Sales Report peso-for-peso, continuously.
Item master (catalog)
The full catalog in-app: prices, barcodes, deal definitions (buy+free=set price), and CPR/FDA registration fields.
Drift check: ⚠ flags any price that differs from Shopify right now — review before the pricing cutover.
Costs and margin % are visible to you (finance + admin only — hidden from every other role).
Until the pricing switch flips, the master runs in shadow: Shopify remains pricing truth.
Recall trace & product registrations

Batch recall trace (Logistics): type a SKU/batch → every clinic that received it with dates and quantities — OUT-sheet history plus ledger picks, so it survives the sheet’s retirement. Printable contact list in seconds.

Product registrations (Inventory): CPR/FDA type, number, expiry per SKU. Expired shows red (“EXPIRED Nd ago”), within 6 months amber countdown — both float to the top. Edit via the row link (rides item-master permissions).
Approvals — the control gate

Specialist orders that cross the account’s credit limit (finance-set) or the company approval threshold (super-admin flag) save as HELD: invisible to the warehouse, waiting in Sales & CRM → Approvals.
You read the Approvals queue (decisions are managers’/admin’s) — watch how your limits behave in practice.
The inventory command center
Dashboard: KPI cards, running-out-in-30-days, category split, out-of-stock commercial, expiring-in-3-months.
Action center: everything needing action today, prioritized — the daily to-do.
All SKUs: sortable master list; tap for the product drawer (batches, 13-month trend, deals, forecast).
Alerts: out of stock · low stock · negative stock · expiry tracker · reorder alerts — each with exact SKUs and quantities.
Planning: stockout forecast (trend + seasonal velocity) · stock coverage · reorder plan · reorder point · demand variability (CV classes) · ABC analysis · write-off forecast.
Batch view: every batch with expiry and bin, FEFO-ordered — the same data behind pick lists and recall.
Data health: feed freshness, price≠Shopify and stock≠Shopify reconciliation — the system tells you when to distrust its own feed.
Finance views: aged inventory · shrinkage tracker · cash in expiring stock — inventory as money. Logistics views: Remedy branch shipments log · branch expiry watch.
Every view: plain-language description, “how is this calculated”, CSV export, full peso figures.
Sales analytics — the scoreboard
Sales overview: units and value for any period (today → 12 months → custom), split deals vs à-la-carte vs true giveaways, charts included.
Sales vs target: monthly attainment by total, brand line, product, and specialist — the 245-row corporate target file, or in-app targets when set.
Per-specialist drill-downs and profile pages with month calendars.
Field coverage: contacts/day, accounts reached vs the whole universe, not-reached ranked by value.
Vs accounting: continuous peso-for-peso reconciliation to the official Sales Report.
Leaderboard & pace: MTD race + projected month-end attainment per specialist — the mid-month coaching tool.

Baked-in conventions: deal +1s are deal units (not free); “free” = ₱0 outside any deal; pull-outs and TEST never count as sales; native orders fold into sales totals only at cutover (no double counting).
With or without Remedy
Remedy is a sister company and one of our customers, and Healthspan also sells to its own staff and academy. Accounting’s Sales Booked leaves both out.
So every sales view opens on External only — third-party sales, the same population accounting counts. The toolbar switch flips the whole page to Incl. Remedy when you want the full picture.

It is one setting across all the sales views, the booked chip on your home page and the Accounts list, so those pages can never show you two different answers. Every figure is labelled with which population it is.
The setting is yours, on this device, like the period and product-line filters.

On the Accounts list, External only subtracts each clinic’s internal orders rather than hiding the clinic — only an account whose every order was internal drops off the list. So a real clinic that once had an order mis-tagged still shows, minus that order.

TARGETS AND COMMISSIONS — Targets and commissions are the exception: they always count external sales only, whatever the toggle says. A target is set on third-party sales and commission is paid on them, so Remedy and internal orders never move either number.
Forecasting & the AI layer
Stockout forecast: trend + seasonal velocity per SKU; campaign windows banner it so promos stop being surprises.
Forecast accuracy (MAPE): each month’s forecast is frozen automatically, then scored against actual movement — MAPE and bias per month, worst misses ranked. The forecast grades itself.
AI planning review: one click walks every SKU, campaigns, and recent misses → an exception report with 5 prioritized actions and quantities.
Ask AI: plain-language questions over live inventory and sales, in-app or Slack (/stock), any hour.
When the bell pings you
The bell pings only the person who ACTS — nobody is copied on someone else’s action items. The queues themselves are always open in-app for anyone with access.

What to do
Where it takes you

Statement out; the owner is pinged too

Watch the decision; adjust policy if needed

blocks.v: Business review — the monthly report, generated

Sales analytics → Business review: the monthly sales performance report computed from HQ — at a glance, brands vs target with a 13-month chart, products per brand, machines and demo units, accounts monitoring, clients & buying behaviour, one panel per specialist, then the plan. Pick the month at the top; figures are external sales only, as on Targets.

Every section is readable; the commentary boxes are written by the sales manager and by each specialist, so on this page they are view-only for you. The figures are the same as Targets and Scorecards — external sales only.
The finance week
Daily: payments and cheque statuses as they happen — the credit gate reads your ledger live.
Monday: Cash-flow forecast; deposit due cheques.
Midweek: AR red bucket — chase list.
Month end: freeze the valuation → Commissions CSV → payroll → accounting export → QBO → tell the super admin the month can be closed.
Ongoing: keep credit limits current.

Something looks wrong? Check Data health first (feed freshness and reconciliation), then tell the super admin. The app ships improvements weekly — if a step in this manual moved, it moved somewhere better.
